posts.title: Why Localdesk exists
posts.caption:
I'm a construction project manager. I've watched good tradespeople lose jobs because the phone rang while they were up a ladder or under a sink.

So I started Localdesk in Saltash: an AI receptionist called Mia that can answer the calls you can't, take the caller's details and text them to you, plus Books, a simple way to keep receipts and invoices in your own accounting software.

We're just getting started, and I'd love to hear how you handle missed calls today.

Want to see Mia in action? {LINK}

posts.title: On the roof, phone ringing
posts.caption:
You're on a roof. The phone rings. You can't answer.

Mia is an AI receptionist that can pick up when you can't, take the caller's name, address and what's wrong, and text you the details so you can ring back already knowing the job.

You keep your own number. 7-day free trial.

posts.title: How Mia works in three steps
posts.caption:
How it works, in three steps:
1. We set Mia up around your business, services and area.
2. You forward your calls when you can't pick up. You keep your number.
3. A text lands with who called and what they need.

Callers are told the call may be recorded, and calls are transcribed, so anything unclear can be checked.
{LINK}
posts.brief: Text tile with three numbered steps.
posts.gbp: How Mia works: we set her up around your business, you forward calls when you can't answer, and a text arrives with who called and what they need. You keep your number.

posts.title: She is an AI, and says so
posts.caption:
Mia is an AI, and she says so.

She takes details and passes them on. She doesn't give quotes, book your diary or promise times. You call back and win the work.

We'd rather be upfront than have a customer feel tricked.
{LINK}

posts.title: Five questions to ask first
posts.caption:
Five questions to ask any answering service before you sign:
1. Does it say it's an AI or a person?
2. Do I keep my own number?
3. Is it set up around my business?
4. Can I read what was said on a call?
5. Can I try it first?

We're happy to answer all five for Mia.
{LINK}

posts.title: Tip: voicemail greeting
posts.caption:
Voicemail greeting tip: say your name, your trade, and what to leave: name, number, address, job. It saves you ringing people back to ask the basics.

Or let Mia ask for you.
